overview.definition: Mastitis is an inflammatory condition of the udder in dairy cows, usually caused by bacterial infection.
overview.subclinical: Subclinical mastitis has no visible symptoms in milk or udder, but leads to increased Somatic Cell Count (SCC) and reduced milk yield. Early detection is critical.
overview.clinical: Clinical mastitis shows visible symptoms like swelling, redness, heat, pain in the udder, and abnormal milk (clots, flakes, or watery milk).

early_symptoms: Slight rise in udder surface temperature detected via thermal imaging
Minor swelling or localized udder warmth
Early subtle changes in milk yield
Elevated somatic cell levels before visible milk alterations
safety_disclaimer: IMPORTANT: Gau Rakshak provides early risk forecasting and risk alerts only. It DOES NOT provide confirmed medical diagnoses, nor does it recommend medicines or dosages. If high risk is detected, immediate examination by a qualified veterinarian is recommended.
prevention: Maintain clean and dry teats and stall bedding
Ensure proper milking machine vacuum calibration
Regular udder health monitoring using Gau Rakshak thermal and spectral sensors
